- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.11) and prices are trending upward, model often over-anticipates; reduce forecast peak or delay upward move.  
- Model frequently over-estimates short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high) and under-estimates subsequent pullback; apply a 1–2 day lag correction after spikes.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model under-estimates true price range in 70% of cases; add 2–5% buffer to forecast mean when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to “smooth” them out; increase volatility in forecast to reflect sentiment-driven noise.
